raw_response:
This sorghum plot is small, only about a quarter of my land, but sorghum is our food crop so I must take care of it. I went to school a little, so I know the cooperative sells DAP and urea, but one bag of DAP costs real money and my plot is tiny — I will buy just a small share, maybe split a bag with my brother who also plants sorghum nearby. I keep two oxen and some goats, so I have manure from the kraal that I will spread before ploughing; that is what my father always did and it still helps. I will keep my own sorghum seed from last harvest like most of my neighbors — the improved seed at the co-op is more for maize, and for sorghum the local one handles our dry spells better.
